venues.name: Bulgari Hotel Tokyo
venues.note: Italian jewellery-house glamour suspended in the clouds above Tokyo Station, the city's most-lauded address of the moment.
credentials: World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 15, highest in Japan)

venues.name: Aman Tokyo
venues.note: Aman's first city house, a washi-and-stone sanctuary poised above the financial district, silence six floors deep.

venues.name: Janu Tokyo
venues.note: Aman's warmer, more sociable sibling, eight restaurants and one of the city's largest wellness floors, in the new Azabudai quarter.

venues.name: Palace Hotel Tokyo
venues.note: A serene, family-owned house looking straight onto the Imperial Palace moat, old-Tokyo grace, quietly perfected.

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Otemachi
venues.note: The surest hands in the city, high over the Imperial gardens, home to Est and the celebrated Virtù bar.

venues.name: The Peninsula Tokyo
venues.note: A landmark corner facing the Imperial Palace and Hibiya Park, Peninsula polish, with the city's grandest lobby tea.

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo
venues.note: The highest rooms in the city, crowning Tokyo Midtown, the skyline unrolls beneath your window.

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental, Tokyo
venues.note: The group's quiet precision above old-merchant Nihonbashi, a house of light, art and view.

venues.name: The Capitol Hotel Tokyu
venues.note: Shoji screens, natural wood and a garden pond beside Hie Shrine, a true urban oasis, run with rare grace.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2025, five consecutive years)

venues.name: Hoshinoya Tokyo
venues.note: A modern ryokan stacked into a tower, you leave your shoes at the door and the city at the pavement.

venues.name: The Okura Tokyo
venues.note: Mid-century Japanese modernism, faithfully rebuilt, the lantern lobby is a design pilgrimage in its own right.

venues.name: Andaz Tokyo Toranomon Hills
venues.note: A design-led sky house atop Toranomon Hills, with one of the city's best rooftop bars and views to match.

venues.name: Shangri-La Tokyo
venues.note: Chandeliered Asian grandeur directly above Tokyo Station, glamour with the platform at your feet.

venues.name: Fairmont Tokyo
venues.note: Fairmont's Japan debut, high in the Blue Front Shibaura tower, with commanding views over Tokyo Bay.

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi
venues.note: A small, jewel-like Four Seasons over the rail lines, and the address of three-Michelin-lauded Sézanne.

venues.name: The Prince Gallery Tokyo Kioicho, a Luxury Collection Hotel
venues.note: High-floor rooms with a glass-walled sky lobby, one of the great value skyline views in the city.

venues.name: The Tokyo Station Hotel
venues.note: A restored 1915 red-brick landmark inside the station itself, European classicism at the heart of Tokyo.

venues.name: The Aoyama Grand Hotel
venues.note: Retro-modern glamour in the fashion district, a design house for members who came to shop and be seen.

venues.name: Bellustar Tokyo, A Pan Pacific Hotel
venues.note: The top floors of Shinjuku's tallest tower, the neon city spread out far below.

venues.name: The Prince Sakura Tower Tokyo, a Luxury Collection Hotel
venues.note: A low-rise house set in a historic Japanese garden, cherry trees, teahouses and quiet, near Shinagawa.

venues.name: Hotel New Otani Tokyo, Executive House Zen
venues.note: A serene, service-led wing looking over a 400-year-old garden, the best of a storied Tokyo institution.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2025, Executive House Zen)

venues.name: Conrad Tokyo
venues.note: A crisp, contemporary tower with wide views over Hamarikyu Gardens and Tokyo Bay.

venues.name: Grand Hyatt Tokyo
venues.note: Warm, grown-up luxury in the heart of Roppongi Hills, dining and galleries on the doorstep.

venues.name: Park Hyatt Tokyo
venues.note: The city's most cinematic hotel, the New York Grill and Bar on the 52nd floor, above the clouds.

venues.name: The Tokyo EDITION, Toranomon
venues.note: Kengo Kuma-designed calm with a forest lobby and a rooftop bar the city talks about.

venues.name: The Tokyo EDITION, Ginza
venues.note: EDITION's second Tokyo house, dropped into the middle of Ginza, greenery, glass and quiet cool.

venues.name: Hyatt Centric Ginza Tokyo
venues.note: A smart, well-located Ginza house for members who want the address without the icon's price.

venues.name: Keio Plaza Hotel Tokyo
venues.note: A large, capable Shinjuku classic, dependable comfort with pools and plenty of dining.

venues.name: Hilton Tokyo
venues.note: A reliable, roomy Shinjuku tower, easy, central and generous for a family on the move.

venues.name: The Strings by InterContinental Tokyo
venues.note: A glass sky-lobby above Shinagawa station, quiet luxury with the bullet trains at your feet.

venues.name: Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel
venues.note: High-floor calm above the roar of Shibuya, the crossing below, the city beyond.

venues.name: Hotel Chinzanso Tokyo
venues.note: A grand hotel in a famous camellia garden, waterfalls, a pagoda, and evening mist among the trees.

venues.name: The Gate Hotel Asakusa Kaminarimon by Hulic
venues.note: A rooftop terrace looking straight at Senso-ji and the Skytree, old Tokyo, from above.

venues.name: Trunk (Hotel) Yoyogi Park
venues.note: A small Japanese-Danish house on the edge of an urban forest, design-forward and quietly green.

venues.name: K5
venues.note: Swedish design and warm concrete in a converted 1920s bank, the city's most characterful boutique stay.

venues.name: Hotel Ryumeikan Tokyo
venues.note: A warm, well-run house blending Japanese hospitality with an unbeatable station-side address.

venues.name: Sézanne
venues.note: Classical French rewritten with a light hand and Japanese ingredients, Tokyo's highest-ranked table in the world.

venues.name: Narisawa
venues.note: 'Satoyama' cooking that plates the Japanese landscape itself, forest, sea and soil, in sequence.

venues.name: Florilège
venues.note: Chef Hiroyasu Kawate's theatrical, sustainability-driven French, reborn in the new Azabudai quarter.

venues.name: Den
venues.note: The warmest kitchen in Tokyo, Zaiyu Hasegawa's playful, generous kaiseki, served with a grin.

venues.name: Nihonryori RyuGin
venues.note: Seiji Yamamoto's science-meets-tradition kaiseki, one of Japan's defining fine-dining rooms.

venues.name: Kanda
venues.note: Pure, unshowy kaiseki that has held three stars since the guide began, restraint as mastery.

venues.name: Quintessence
venues.note: No printed menu, complete trust, Shuzo Kishida's exacting French, unchanged in its pursuit of the perfect.

venues.name: L'Effervescence
venues.note: Shinobu Namae's nature-led French, quietly philosophical, deeply Japanese in spirit.

venues.name: Sazenka
venues.note: The only Chinese restaurant in Japan to hold three stars, Chinese technique read through a Japanese lens.

venues.name: L'Osier
venues.note: Shiseido's grand French salon in Ginza, old-world luxury, three stars, faultless service.

venues.name: Joël Robuchon (Gastronomy)
venues.note: The late master's flagship château, grand, gilded French dining that has held three stars from the start.

venues.name: Kagurazaka Ishikawa
venues.note: Intimate, seasonal kaiseki down a lantern-lit lane, three stars, and only a handful of seats.

venues.name: Azabu Kadowaki
venues.note: Playful, truffle-laced kaiseki from a chef who cooks exactly as he pleases, and holds three stars for it.

venues.name: Kohaku
venues.note: Koji Koizumi's refined, precise kaiseki, one of the quiet three-star greats.

venues.name: Sushi Saito
venues.note: Long held to be the finest sushi counter in Tokyo, and the hardest seat in the city to secure.

venues.name: Maz
venues.note: Virgilio Martínez's Peru-to-Japan altitude cooking, the Lima phenomenon, translated to Tokyo.

venues.name: Crony
venues.note: Modern, ingredient-led fine dining with a superb pairing programme, refined without ceremony.

venues.name: Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongi
venues.note: The Jiro lineage, at the more reachable Roppongi counter, sushi as devotion.

venues.name: Sushi Kanesaka
venues.note: A benchmark Ginza edomae counter, classical, exact, and quietly warm.

venues.name: Esquisse
venues.note: Bright, delicate contemporary French high above Ginza, a room full of light and precision.

venues.name: Akasaka Kikunoi
venues.note: The Kyoto kaiseki dynasty's Tokyo house, seasonal Japanese cooking of great poise.

venues.name: Tempura Kondo
venues.note: The temple of vegetable tempura, feather-light, and unlike tempura anywhere else.

venues.name: Ginza Koju
venues.note: Understated, seasonal Ginza kaiseki from a chef's chef, quiet excellence, two stars.

venues.name: Édition Koji Shimomura
venues.note: Precise, seasonal French from a chef trained under the greats, measured and refined.

venues.name: Ginza Shinohara
venues.note: A Nagano-born chef's exacting kaiseki, the dashi alone is worth the journey.

venues.name: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon
venues.note: The counter concept that changed fine dining, small plates, open kitchen, red-and-black theatre.

venues.name: Ryuzu
venues.note: Generous, classical French with a warm room and famously fair value for the level.

venues.name: Beige Alain Ducasse Tokyo
venues.note: Ducasse's Chanel-topped Ginza salon, French cooking with a couturier's polish.

venues.name: Ode
venues.note: Yusuke Namai's contemporary French, inventive, personal and warmly run.

venues.name: Sugalabo
venues.note: Yosuke Suga's membership-driven, no-menu counter, the city's most coveted contemporary table.

venues.name: Tempura Motoyoshi
venues.note: A serene tempura counter that climbed to two stars, course after course, impossibly light.

venues.name: Nabeno-Ism
venues.note: Riverside French from a Robuchon protégé, with the Skytree framed in the window.

venues.name: Ristorante Aso
venues.note: Refined, produce-led Italian in a leafy villa, one of Tokyo's most gracious Italian rooms.

venues.name: Faro
venues.note: Shiseido's rooftop Italian, plant-forward, seasonal and quietly progressive.

venues.name: Ginza Kojyu
venues.note: Seasonal Japanese cooking of quiet confidence, at the heart of Ginza.

venues.name: Nakajima
venues.note: A one-star kitchen whose sardine lunches are among the great bargains in Tokyo dining.

venues.name: Kabi
venues.note: A young, Nordic-influenced kitchen and natural-wine list that quietly became a Tokyo favourite.

venues.name: Nakiryu
venues.note: The tantanmen that put a ramen shop on the world's radar, worth every minute of the queue.

venues.name: Japanese Soba Noodles Tsuta
venues.note: The first ramen shop in the world to win a Michelin star, truffle-scented shoyu, still exceptional.

venues.name: Ginza Kagari
venues.note: A silky chicken-paitan ramen down a Ginza alley, the bowl that converts the sceptics.

venues.name: Tonkatsu Narikura
venues.note: Regarded by many as the finest tonkatsu in Japan, worth the trek out of the centre.

venues.name: Tachiguisushi Sushikawa
venues.note: Stand-up sushi of real quality, counter chat, top fish, none of the ceremony.

venues.name: Bird Land
venues.note: The yakitori counter that made grilled chicken a fine art, every part of the bird, perfectly charred.

venues.name: Afuri
venues.note: The yuzu-shio ramen that became a Tokyo signature, light, citrus-bright, endlessly copied.

venues.name: Bar Benfiddich
venues.note: A no-menu apothecary bar where the cocktails are built from herbs the bartender grows himself.

venues.name: The Bellwood
venues.note: A Taisho-era-styled bar reimagining kaiseki as cocktails, playful, precise, deeply Tokyo.

venues.name: The SG Club
venues.note: Shingo Gokan's genre-bending drinking den, 'Guzzle' below, 'Sip' above, both excellent.

venues.name: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise-dori
venues.note: Tokyo's oldest temple (645 AD); walk under the giant red Kaminarimon lantern, then the Nakamise craft-and-snack lane to the incense-wreathed main hall. Go at dawn or after 8pm for the empty, lantern-lit version.

venues.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
venues.note: A vast, hushed forest of 100,000 donated trees around Emperor Meiji's shrine, five minutes from Harajuku's chaos. Sunday mornings you may catch a traditional Shinto wedding procession.

venues.name: Zojo-ji Temple with Tokyo Tower
venues.note: A grand Tokugawa-family temple framed perfectly against the orange Tokyo Tower behind it - the city's best temple-plus-tower photograph, and rows of tiny Jizo statues in the garden.

venues.name: Nezu Shrine
venues.note: A 1900-year-old shrine with a tunnel of vermilion torii gates (a serene, uncrowded alternative to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari) and an azalea garden that erupts in colour each April.

venues.name: Gotokuji Temple (the beckoning-cat temple)
venues.note: Reputed birthplace of the maneki-neko; hundreds of white waving-cat figures line the racks in a quiet suburban temple. A charming, offbeat stop children love.

venues.name: teamLab Borderless, Azabudai Hills
venues.note: The reborn 'borderless' digital-art world (reopened at Azabudai Hills in 2024 after leaving Odaiba) - rooms with no maps where artworks flow between spaces. Book timed tickets well ahead; your advisor can secure a quiet slot.

venues.name: teamLab Planets TOKYO
venues.note: The barefoot, wade-through-water immersive counterpart near Toyosu (extended through 2027) - you walk into knee-deep koi-projection water and mirrored infinity gardens. Wear rollable trousers; hugely popular, so pre-book.

venues.name: Mori Art Museum & Tokyo City View
venues.note: Ambitious contemporary shows on the 53rd floor, paired with a wraparound observation deck - culture and skyline in one ticket, open late into the evening.

venues.name: Nezu Museum
venues.note: Kengo Kuma's serene building of pre-modern Asian art, but the real draw is the hidden strolling garden of stone lanterns and teahouses - a green pause steps off luxury Omotesando.

venues.name: Tokyo National Museum
venues.note: Japan's oldest and largest museum; the Honkan gallery walks you through samurai armour, swords, ukiyo-e and ceramics in one graceful sweep. The place to grasp the whole arc of Japanese art.

venues.name: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
venues.note: Miyazaki's whimsical museum with an exclusive short film, the Catbus and rooftop robot soldier. Strictly advance-reservation only (tickets released monthly and sell out in minutes) - have your advisor book the instant they open.

venues.name: Ota Memorial Museum of Ukiyo-e Art
venues.note: An intimate museum devoted entirely to woodblock prints - Hokusai, Hiroshige, Utamaro - with rotating themed shows. Small, uncrowded and deeply rewarding for a couple of quiet hours.

venues.name: Shibuya Crossing & Hachiko
venues.note: The world's busiest pedestrian scramble - thousands cross at once under the neon. Watch from the Starbucks window or Mag's Park rooftop, and greet the loyal-dog Hachiko statue nearby.

venues.name: Shibuya Sky
venues.note: An open-air rooftop deck 230m up with a glass-edge sky corner and hammocks - the most cinematic sunset-into-neon view in the city. Book the sunset slot ahead; it goes fast.

venues.name: Tokyo Skytree
venues.note: At 634m the tallest tower in Japan, with two glass observation decks over the endless grey sprawl to Mt. Fuji on clear days. The base holds the Solamachi mall and an aquarium for families.

venues.name: Tokyo Tower
venues.note: The 1958 Eiffel-inspired orange icon, still beloved and beautifully lit at night. Less about the view than the nostalgia; best admired from Zojo-ji or a nearby rooftop bar.

venues.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observatory
venues.note: A free 202m observation deck in Kenzo Tange's twin-tower city hall - a smart no-cost skyline view, plus the nightly 'Tokyo Night & Light' projection show on the facade.

venues.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
venues.note: A vast garden blending French formal, English landscape and Japanese strolling styles - Tokyo's finest cherry-blossom lawn in spring and a serene escape from Shinjuku's density any season.

venues.name: Rikugien Garden
venues.note: An exquisite Edo-era strolling garden built around a central pond recreating scenes from classical poetry - autumn maple illuminations here are among the city's most beautiful evenings.

venues.name: Hama-rikyu Gardens & tea house
venues.note: A former shogun's seaside garden with a tidal pond, framed against Shiodome skyscrapers; take matcha and a wagashi sweet at the pond-island Nakajima teahouse. Arrive by the Sumida river boat.

venues.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
venues.note: Free-to-enter grounds of the former Edo Castle - climb the old keep foundation for city views, wander the moats and stone walls at the literal centre of Tokyo.

venues.name: Kiyosumi Teien Garden
venues.note: A jewel-box strolling garden of stepping-stones across a koi pond and rare landscape rocks, in Tokyo's third-wave-coffee district - pair it with a flat white in a warehouse cafe nearby.

venues.name: Ueno Park & its museums
venues.note: A sprawling park holding the National Museum, Western Art museum, science museum, a zoo and Shinobazu lotus pond - the densest culture cluster in the city, glorious under cherry blossom.

venues.name: Shibuya district wander
venues.note: Beyond the crossing: the sleek Miyashita Park, the alleys of Nonbei Yokocho, and Shibuya's new towers. Youth-energy central, best explored on foot from late afternoon into the neon evening.

venues.name: Shinjuku & Golden Gai / Omoide Yokocho
venues.note: Neon canyons, the tiny-bar warren of Golden Gai and the smoky yakitori lane of Omoide Yokocho ('Memory Lane'). Atmospheric and cinematic; an advisor can pre-arrange a table in the good ones.

venues.name: Harajuku - Takeshita & Cat Streets
venues.note: Japan's youth-fashion crucible: candy-coloured Takeshita Street for the spectacle, quieter Cat Street and Ura-Harajuku backstreets for the actual good boutiques and coffee.

venues.name: Ginza stroll
venues.note: Tokyo's grand shopping boulevard of flagship maisons and department stores; on weekend afternoons the main avenue closes to traffic and becomes a 'pedestrian paradise'. Best paired with a depachika lunch.

venues.name: Yanaka old-town wander
venues.note: One of the few districts to survive the war and quakes - low wooden houses, artisan shops, a rambling cemetery of cherry trees and the shitamachi (old downtown) atmosphere Tokyo mostly lost.

venues.name: Shimokitazawa
venues.note: A low-rise, car-free maze of vintage shops, indie cafes, record stores and tiny theatres - Tokyo's bohemian heart, best on a slow weekend afternoon with no plan.

venues.name: Kagurazaka
venues.note: A former geisha quarter of cobbled slopes and hidden ryotei restaurants, with a French accent from its expat community - discreet, refined and lovely for an evening walk to dinner.

venues.name: Nakameguro & the Meguro River
venues.note: A canal lined with cherry trees, boutiques and the flagship Starbucks Reserve Roastery. Peak magic during sakura season when the river glows with lanterns; chic and calm the rest of the year.

venues.name: Koenji
venues.note: Retro, gritty and unpolished - vintage clothing, live-music dives and standing bars, plus the huge Awa-Odori dance festival in August. Real, un-touristed Tokyo counter-culture.

venues.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
venues.note: The inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market thrives - grazing stalls of tamago, uni, grilled scallops, knives and dashi. Go hungry by 9am; ask about veg-friendly stalls.

venues.name: Toyosu Market tuna auction
venues.note: The successor to Tsukiji's famous auction - watch the pre-dawn tuna bidding from a viewing deck (advance application for the ground-floor window), then eat the freshest sushi breakfast in Tokyo.

venues.name: Ameyoko Market
venues.note: A raucous open-air bazaar under the train tracks - seafood, spices, sneakers and cheap eats shouted from every stall. The closest Tokyo gets to a South-Asian-style street market, and fun with kids.

venues.name: Depachika food hall grazing
venues.note: The basement food halls of Isetan Shinjuku, Mitsukoshi Ginza or Takashimaya are gastronomic theatre - jewel-like sweets, pristine bento, tea and sake. A refined, air-conditioned way to taste Japan.

venues.name: Grand Sumo tournament, Ryogoku Kokugikan
venues.note: The Tokyo basho runs three times a year (January, May, September). Ringside box seats are electric; between tournaments an advisor can arrange a morning stable practice visit instead.

venues.name: Kabuki matinee at Kabukiza
venues.note: Japan's premier kabuki theatre - stylised drama, dazzling costumes and the hanamichi runway through the audience. English earphone guides make it accessible; single-act tickets suit a first taste.

venues.name: Private tea ceremony
venues.note: A guided chado ceremony - the choreographed whisking and serving of matcha in a tatami room - is one of Japan's most quietly moving experiences. Advisor arranges an English-speaking, private session.

venues.name: Onsen or design sento soak
venues.note: Bathe in mineral waters - the theatrical Oedo-Onsen-style complexes, or beautifully restored neighbourhood sento. A restorative ritual; note tattoo policies, which an advisor can pre-check for you.

venues.name: Omotesando architecture walk
venues.note: A leafy 'Champs-Elysees' lined with flagship boutiques designed by the world's star architects - Prada by Herzog & de Meuron, Dior, Tod's. An open-air museum of contemporary architecture and luxury.

venues.name: Ginza Six & Ginza shopping
venues.note: The district's most ambitious mall, with rotating art installations, a rooftop garden and a hidden Noh theatre, anchoring a walk past Wako, Itoya stationery and every global maison flagship.

venues.name: Akihabara Electric Town
venues.note: The neon capital of anime, manga, gaming and gadgets - multi-storey arcades, retro-game shops and pop-culture excess. Sensory overload in the best way, and unmissable for teens.

venues.name: Nakano Broadway
venues.note: A wonderfully weird retro mall of collectible, vintage-toy, manga and watch shops - Akihabara's older, cultier cousin. A treasure hunt for serious collectors, minus the crowds.

venues.name: Sumida River cruise
venues.note: Glide from Asakusa past a dozen bridges to Hama-rikyu or futuristic Odaiba - including the manga-artist-designed Himiko 'spaceship' boat. A restful way to see the city change from old to new.

venues.name: Todoroki Valley
venues.note: A cool, green ravine walk along a stream, complete with a small temple and teahouse - startlingly rural for central Tokyo, and blissfully quiet. A secret local favourite for a hot day.

venues.name: Kamakura day-trip
venues.note: A seaside former capital of Zen temples, bamboo groves at Hokoku-ji and the open-air Great Buddha of Kotoku-in. Add the Enoshima tram along the coast for a perfect, unhurried day.

venues.name: Nikko day-trip
venues.note: The lavishly carved Toshogu shrine complex - the ornate opposite of Zen restraint - set among cedar forests, waterfalls and Lake Chuzenji in the mountains. A full, rewarding day north of the city.

venues.name: Hakone day-trip
venues.note: Hot-spring resort of ryokan, the Open-Air Museum's sculptures, a pirate-ship lake cruise and Fuji views from the ropeway over sulphur vents. Ideal as an overnight ryokan stay your advisor can book.

venues.name: Yokohama day-trip
venues.note: A breezy harbour city - Japan's largest Chinatown, the Minato Mirai waterfront, the Cup Noodles museum and Sankeien garden. An easy half-day that feels a world away from Tokyo's density.

venues.name: Odaiba & the waterfront
venues.note: A man-made bay island with a Rainbow Bridge skyline view, a Statue-of-Liberty replica, the giant Gundam robot, malls and hot-spring complexes. Family-friendly, and lovely at dusk.

venues.name: Roppongi art triangle
venues.note: The National Art Center's glass wave, the Suntory Museum's craft focus and Mori Art Museum form a walkable trio of world-class shows - the single densest hit of contemporary art in Tokyo.

venues.name: Yoyogi Park
venues.note: Tokyo's great democratic lawn beside Meiji Jingu - rockabilly dancers, picnics, drum circles and space to simply be. On weekends it becomes a free, joyful window into local Tokyo life.

venues.name: Bar Benfiddich
venues.note: An apothecary in the sky, Hiroyasu Kayama builds each drink, no menu, from herbs and roots he grows himself.

venues.name: Virtù
venues.note: A jewel-box lounge high in the Four Seasons, French aperitifs, Japanese spirits, and the skyline through the glass.

venues.name: The Bellwood
venues.note: A Taishō-era drinking den reimagining kaiseki as cocktails, playful, precise and unmistakably Tokyo.

venues.name: The SG Club
venues.note: Shingo Gokan's genre-bending club, 'Guzzle' below for the crowd, 'Sip' above for the connoisseur, both superb.

venues.name: Punch Room
venues.note: EDITION's clubby ode to the punch bowl, retold through sake, yuzu and green tea, warm, low-lit, quietly glamorous.

venues.name: Bar Libre
venues.note: A serious, spirits-deep cocktail room from a celebrated bar group, classical technique, encyclopaedic backbar.

venues.name: Gold Bar at EDITION
venues.note: A gilded, curtained hideaway channelling pre-Prohibition America, opulent, intimate and out of sight of the street.

venues.name: Tokyo Confidential
venues.note: Caviar, champagne and mischievous cocktails with Tokyo Tower framed in the window, a sophisticated house party.

venues.name: Bar High Five
venues.note: Hidetsugu Ueno pours the definitive Ginza cocktail, no menu, no theatrics, just the finest classic in Tokyo.
credentials: Former World's 50 Best Bars (No. 12) & Asia's 50 Best Bars top-tier
The benchmark of the Ginza cocktail tradition

venues.name: Gen Yamamoto
venues.note: Eight seats, a seasonal tasting flight of cocktails built from the day's produce, the omakase of the bar world.
credentials: Regularly named among the world's most singular cocktail experiences

venues.name: The Aubrey
venues.note: A theatrical izakaya-bar on the 41st floor of the Park Hyatt, Eastern flavours, Western swagger, and the skyline entire.
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars honouree (Park Hyatt Tokyo)
One of the city's most celebrated high-floor bars

venues.name: New York Bar
venues.note: The most cinematic bar in Tokyo, jazz, deep leather, and the Shinjuku skyline that fixed the city in the world's mind.
credentials: The 'Lost in Translation' bar, 52nd floor of the Park Hyatt

venues.name: Peter: The Bar
venues.note: A silvery, sculptural room on the Peninsula's 24th floor, Hibiya Park and the Imperial gardens spread below.

venues.name: Bar Trench
venues.note: A tiny, absinthe-scented Ebisu original that helped write Tokyo's modern cocktail story, bohemian and beloved.
credentials: A cornerstone of Tokyo's craft-cocktail movement

venues.name: Bar Orchard Ginza
venues.note: A husband-and-wife counter where you choose a fruit and they compose the drink, inventive, warm, deeply personal.
credentials: A Ginza original known for its fresh-fruit cocktails

venues.name: Star Bar Ginza
venues.note: Hisashi Kishi's temple of the classic, hand-carved ice, flawless technique, and the quiet of true Ginza mastery.
credentials: One of Ginza's most revered classic cocktail bars

venues.name: Andaz Tavern & Rooftop Bar
venues.note: The 52nd-floor terrace atop Toranomon Hills, one of the great open-air perches over the glittering city.
credentials: MICHELIN Key hotel; among Tokyo's best-loved rooftop bars

venues.name: Golden Gai
venues.note: Six alleys of tiny post-war bars, each seating a handful, a warren of old Tokyo that never quite sleeps.
credentials: An iconic surviving quarter of post-war Shinjuku nightlife
